Hi Alice - thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and next steps so we can align on recommended deployment mode (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private):

Summary of your requirements from today:
- SSO: Okta SAML + SCIM for user provisioning across your ops team
- Key management: requirement for customer-controlled KMS and potential HSM key custody for encryption of model artifacts/keys
- Logging & retention: security/legal requires up to 7-year audit logs for inference requests and access logs, with the ability to ship logs to your logging platform (Splunk)
- Data residency: production inference must run in a VPC and restrict egress where possible

High-level guidance on modes (short):
- Hosted API: fastest path to production but we control infrastructure and standard retention/policies; limited for HSM/BYOK scenarios. Good if you can accept vendor-managed KMS and shorter retention windows or push logs to your tenant with integrations.
- Dedicated: reserved capacity in our cloud with tenant isolation. Supports cloud KMS integrations and private networking options in some regions but does not provide on-prem HSM or HSM appliances under your physical control.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): full customer-managed network + KMS/HSM integrations, longest retention controls, and air-gapped options if needed - this maps best to strict KMS/HSM and 7-year retention asks.

Attachments: FintechCo-MAP-v1.pdf (mutual action plan) attached.

Proposed next steps:
1) Technical architecture session: include your security lead + our infra engineer (Dev Patel) and Hannah (security PM). 60-90 min to go over Okta metadata, KMS/HSM requirements, and logging endpoints.
2) Share Okta SAML metadata & SCIM endpoint, and the KMS key policy / contact we should provision for test.
3) We'll follow up with a short doc comparing Dedicated vs Private for the specific constraint set and a draft timeline/estimate.

Are you available for the architecture slot next week (Wed/Thu)? If you prefer we can start with a quick 30-min pre-qual to confirm a few constraints.
